text: Which researcher has earned the title "the Godfather of AI"?
explanation: Hinton spent decades on neural networks while almost nobody else did, including through both of the field's winters, and then supervised the work that produced AlexNet in 2012. He shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics with John Hopfield, and he has been blunt about the safety risks ever since.

text: Which researcher built the ImageNet dataset and has been called the Godmother of AI?
explanation: Li started building ImageNet in 2007 and it is hard to overstate what it did, because most of modern computer vision only became possible once the data existed. She has spent the last several years arguing that the bottleneck has moved from algorithms to data quality, and that the next ImageNet has not been built yet.

text: In 2024, which AI researcher shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on protein structure prediction?
explanation: In 2024 Hassabis and John Jumper shared half the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, and David Baker took the other half for computational protein design. AlphaFold had already predicted the structure of over 200 million proteins by then, which is close to every protein catalogued by hand.

text: Which researcher co-created AlexNet alongside Alex Krizhevsky and Geoffrey Hinton?
explanation: Sutskever was a graduate student at Toronto at the time, and AlexNet is one of the most cited papers in the whole field. He went on to co-found OpenAI, lead the company that made the GPT models, and spend a decade convinced that scaling alone would get to something extraordinary.

text: Which researcher founded DAIR, the Distributed AI Research Institute, and is known for work on algorithmic bias?
explanation: Gebru co-founded Black in AI and led a research team at Google that was pushed out over a paper about the risks of large language models. DAIR came out of that, and the firing became the most public argument anyone in the field has had about what research is allowed to say out loud.

text: Which scholar won the 1978 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences and is known for bounded rationality?
explanation: Simon argued that people satisfice, they look for good enough rather than optimal, and he said the same thing about machines. He and Allen Newell built the Logic Theorist and GPS, and both of them are on the short list of anyone trying to explain where the idea of a thinking machine came from.

text: Who has been the chief executive officer of OpenAI since 2019?
explanation: Altman became CEO in 2019, a year after OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit research lab with the explicit goal of not pursuing profit. That structure has been rewritten twice since, and the board upheaval in November 2023 was the loudest argument anybody has had about who actually controls the company.

text: Which English mathematician designed the Turing test and is regarded as the father of theoretical computer science?
explanation: Turing formalized the idea of a general purpose computing machine and helped break the Enigma code at Bletchley Park. He proposed the imitation game in 1950, and six years later he wrote a paper on machine learning that is the reason the term exists at all.

text: Which researcher was a cofounder and head of Google Brain, and later served as Chief Scientist at Baidu?
explanation: Ng ran Google Brain when the company was largely still using speech and ads research, then spent three years at Baidu before leaving to work on education. He also co-founded Coursera and Deeplearning.ai, which is why his name shows up in far more machine learning course syllabuses than research papers.

text: Which researcher co-founded Anthropic with his sister, and had previously been vice president of research at OpenAI?
explanation: Dario and Daniela Amodei founded Anthropic in January 2021 with the stated goal of promoting AI safety, and he ran research at OpenAI first. Their publishing agenda, Constitutional AI in particular, has been the most sustained public attempt so far to write alignment research down instead of only doing it.

text: Who founded the community blog LessWrong and co-founded the Machine Intelligence Research Institute?
explanation: Yudkowsky founded LessWrong in 2009 using his own posts as seed material, and co-founded MIRI to work on friendly AI. Robin Hanson is the tempting miss because he co-wrote the predecessor blog Overcoming Bias, but he kept that blog while Yudkowsky launched LessWrong. Yudkowsky also spread rationalist ideas through the fanfiction novel Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality.

text: Who wrote the 2014 book Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies?
explanation: Bostrom, then at Oxford, published Superintelligence in 2014 and it became a New York Times bestseller that carried AI risk into the mainstream. Yudkowsky is the closest miss because his writing on intelligence explosion influenced the book, but he never wrote it. The paperclip maximizer thought experiment comes from Bostrom's work on the orthogonality thesis.

text: Who developed convolutional neural networks in the 1980s and served as Meta chief AI scientist?
explanation: LeCun invented convolutional networks at Bell Labs in the late 1980s, including the LeNet system for reading handwritten checks. Hinton is the tempting miss because he shared the 2018 Turing Award with LeCun and Bengio, but his fame rests on backpropagation and deep belief nets rather than CNNs. LeCun joined Facebook in 2013 to found FAIR and served as chief AI scientist for a decade.

text: Who founded the Quebec AI institute Mila and shared the 2018 Turing Award with Hinton and LeCun?
explanation: Bengio founded Mila, the Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute in Montreal, and split the 2018 Turing Award for deep learning breakthroughs. Hassabis is the closest miss because he is another famous lab leader, but he co-founded DeepMind and won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry instead. Bengio also co-directs the CIFAR Learning in Machines and Brains program with LeCun.

text: Who led Tesla Autopilot vision as director of AI and later became known for the Zero to Hero neural network videos?
explanation: Karpathy, an OpenAI founding member, joined Tesla in 2017 and led the Autopilot vision team until 2022. George Hotz is the tempting miss because he also worked briefly with Musk on driving automation, but he founded comma.ai instead of leading Tesla AI. Karpathy returned to OpenAI in 2023 and later founded the AI education company Eureka Labs in 2024.

text: Which OpenAI CTO became interim CEO immediately after Sam Altman was fired in November 2023?
explanation: Murati, OpenAI CTO since 2022, stepped in as interim CEO on November 17 2023 when the board removed Altman. Emmett Shear is the tempting miss because he held the same interim title days later, but he came from Twitch and was second in the sequence. Murati left OpenAI in September 2024 and founded Thinking Machines Lab in February 2025.

text: Who co-founded Mistral AI in 2023 and serves as its CEO after working at DeepMind Paris?
explanation: Mensch left DeepMind Paris in May 2023 and co-founded Mistral AI with Guillaume Lample and Timothee Lacroix, becoming CEO. Lample is the tempting miss because he is also a Mistral co-founder, but he serves as chief scientist rather than CEO. Under Mensch, Mistral released open-weight models like Mistral 7B and Mixtral and became the flagship of European AI.

text: Who founded the Chinese AI company DeepSeek after building the High-Flyer quantitative hedge fund?
explanation: Liang co-founded the quant fund High-Flyer in 2015 and launched DeepSeek in 2023, funding it from the fund and stockpiling Nvidia chips before export controls. Kai-Fu Lee is the tempting miss because he is the other famous Chinese AI founder-investor, but his company is 01.AI rather than DeepSeek. DeepSeek stunned markets in early 2025 when its R1 reasoning model matched Western rivals at far lower reported cost.

text: Who co-founded DeepMind and Inflection AI and became CEO of Microsoft AI in 2024?
explanation: Suleyman co-founded DeepMind in 2010, left Google in 2022 to co-found Inflection AI, then joined Microsoft in March 2024 to lead Copilot and consumer AI. Shane Legg is the tempting miss because he is the third DeepMind co-founder, but he stayed in research rather than taking the Microsoft role. Suleyman also wrote the 2023 book The Coming Wave about AI risk.

text: Which Transformer co-author left Google to found Character.AI and returned to Google in 2024?
explanation: Shazeer, a Google researcher since 2000 who designed key parts of the Transformer, left in 2021 with Daniel De Freitas to found Character.AI. Llion Jones is the tempting miss because he is another Transformer author who left Google for a startup, but he joined Sakana AI in Tokyo rather than founding Character.AI. Google brought Shazeer back in August 2024 with a licensing deal reported at over 2 billion dollars.

text: Which Transformer paper co-author went on to co-found and lead Cohere as CEO?
explanation: Gomez was a 20-year-old intern at Google Brain when he co-authored Attention Is All You Need in 2017, then co-founded Cohere in 2019 as CEO. Illia Polosukhin is the tempting miss because he is another Transformer author turned founder, but he founded NEAR Protocol rather than Cohere. Cohere focuses on enterprise AI models rather than consumer chatbots.

text: Who succeeded Mira Murati as OpenAI interim CEO during the November 2023 leadership crisis?
explanation: Shear, who co-founded Justin.tv and led Twitch as CEO until 2023, accepted the interim job on November 20 after Murati and left when Altman was reinstated days later. Bret Taylor is the tempting miss because he became board chair in the shake-up, but he never held the CEO title. Shear had publicly estimated a 5 to 50 percent chance of AI-caused doom, which drew attention during his brief tenure.

text: Which leather-jacketed executive has led Nvidia as CEO since co-founding it in 1993?
explanation: Huang founded Nvidia with two Sun colleagues and never left, riding gaming graphics into the AI boom in his trademark leather jacket. Morris Chang is the tempting miss because TSMC fabs Nvidia's chips, but he never ran Nvidia.

text: Who became CEO of AMD in 2014 and led its turnaround?
explanation: Su bet AMD on Zen and high-performance chiplets, taking it from near-bankruptcy to datacenter contender. Rory Read is the tempting miss because he was her immediate predecessor as CEO, but the turnaround belongs to Su.

text: Who became CEO of Microsoft in 2014 and backed OpenAI with billions?
explanation: Nadella pivoted Microsoft to cloud-first and placed the $1 billion 2019 bet on OpenAI that grew into the defining AI partnership. Steve Ballmer is the tempting miss because he was the previous CEO, but the OpenAI deal is Nadella's era.

text: Which OpenAI co-founder left the lab and founded xAI in 2023?
explanation: Musk co-founded OpenAI in 2015, departed in 2018, and launched xAI with its Grok chatbot in 2023. Sam Altman is the tempting miss because he is the famous OpenAI face, but he stayed as CEO while Musk left and competed.

text: Before co-founding Google Brain, Jeff Dean had already helped build which Google system for processing data at a scale nobody had attempted?
explanation: MapReduce, with Jeffrey Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat, is the distributed computation technique that let Google index the web by splitting work across thousands of machines. He then co-founded Google Brain in 2011 and became Google's chief scientist, so he shows up twice in AI history for two unrelated reasons.

text: Who is the first author of the 2015 ResNet paper on deep residual learning?
explanation: He led the Microsoft Research Asia team whose skip connections let networks train hundreds of layers deep. Xiangyu Zhang is the tempting miss because he is the second author, but the paper opens with He, Zhang, Ren and Sun in that order.

text: Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993, and the meetings where the business plan was written happened in a roadside diner in East San Jose. Which restaurant chain was it?
explanation: Huang washed dishes and waited tables at a Denny's through his teens in Oregon, so when he needed somewhere quiet with cheap coffee for the 1992 planning meetings he picked the same chain, and Nvidia was founded from a breakfast booth. The company's first capital was $600, split three ways out of the founders' pockets.

text: Lisa Su led AMD's largest-ever purchase, announced in 2020 and completed in February 2022, to bring programmable logic into the chip lineup. Which company did AMD buy?
explanation: Xilinx built the first commercially viable FPGA, and buying it gave AMD the programmable logic behind the adaptive-computing parts it now sells against Nvidia. Altera is the tempting miss because it was the other FPGA pioneer, but that company ended up inside Intel, and AMD's attempt to buy Arm instead collapsed in 2022.

text: Microsoft's AI bet began with a $1 billion investment in 2019, made under the CEO who had taken over that year, and the total has since passed $13 billion. Which company has taken the money?
explanation: Nadella arrived in 2014 after a decade of mobile bets that had not worked, then put $1 billion into OpenAI in 2019 in exchange for Azure becoming the required home for OpenAI's models. That partnership became the engine behind Copilot. Anthropic is the tempting miss because it is the other lab with giant corporate backers, but those are Amazon and Google.

text: Meta bought a 49% stake in Scale AI for more than $14 billion in 2025 and hired the company's founder to run Meta Superintelligence Labs as its Chief AI Officer. Who is he?
explanation: Wang built Scale AI out of his Stanford dorm at 19, turning data labelling and model evaluation into the business every frontier lab buys from, and the stake Meta bought valued the company at roughly $14.3 billion. Nat Friedman is the tempting miss because he arrived in the same shake-up, but he ran GitHub and took the product job, not the AI one.

text: After the Nobel Prize, Hassabis turned DeepMind's protein work into a separate Alphabet company that uses AlphaFold to hunt for drug targets. What is that company called?
explanation: Hassabis co-founded DeepMind in London in 2010 and shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with John Jumper for protein structure prediction. Isomorphic Labs was announced in November 2021 as a DeepMind spin-off that reuses AlphaFold to find drug targets, and he runs it as CEO while chairing DeepMind. Recursion is the tempting miss because it is a well-known AI drug-discovery company, but it grew out of a different lineage.

text: Which researcher behind AlphaFold was named one of Nature's ten 'people who mattered' in science in 2021?
explanation: Jumper was the first author of the AlphaFold 2 paper Nature published in July 2021, and he shared half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with DeepMind's Demis Hassabis. David Baker is the tempting miss because he took the other half of that prize, for computational protein design, but his work was designing proteins rather than predicting their shapes.

text: The image generator that spent its 2022 open beta inside Discord is run by a founder who had previously co-founded Leap Motion, the gesture-control hardware company. Who is he?
explanation: Holz founded Midjourney in San Francisco, and by the August 2022 open beta he told The Register the company was already profitable, which was unusual for a generative-image startup. Jason Allen is the tempting miss because his AI-generated entry won the digital art prize at the 2022 Colorado State Fair, but Allen wrote the prompt and entered the work rather than building the tool.

text: Hugging Face began in New York in 2016 as a chatbot for teenagers and took its name from a hugging-face emoji. Two of its three French co-founders are Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf. Who is the third?
explanation: The company open-sourced the model behind its chatbot and pivoted into a hub where anyone can publish and download models, which is why most open weights now live there. Emad Mostaque is the tempting miss because he ran the competing Stable Diffusion company, which went the other way and open-sourced everything it made.

text: After Tesla, Andrej Karpathy stopped trying to build the biggest models and in 2024 started a company to teach people how they work. Which AI education company did he found?
explanation: Karpathy's public rebuilds of a language model from scratch, most famously the nanoGPT repository, made him the field's default teacher for how a model is actually trained. Deeplearning.ai is the tempting miss because it is the other famous name in AI courses, but that is Andrew Ng's company, and fast.ai belongs to Jeremy Howard.

text: Which researcher, a co-author of the 2018 Gender Shades audit that found facial-analysis systems perform worst on dark-skinned women, founded the Algorithmic Justice League?
explanation: Buolamwini and Gebru's audit tested commercial systems that police departments were buying, which is what pushed facial-recognition bias into the mainstream. Gebru is the tempting miss because he co-wrote that paper and later founded DAIR after being pushed out of Google, but the Algorithmic Justice League is Buolamwini's, and she frames the problem as an artist as much as a researcher.

text: Which CEO personally delivered the first Nvidia DGX-1 supercomputer to OpenAI in August 2016?
explanation: Huang showed up at OpenAI's office in 2016 with the first DGX-1, built for deep learning, and Elon Musk posted the photo of the handover. Lisa Su is the tempting miss because she runs AMD, Nvidia's closest rival, but in 2016 she had only just started AMD's turnaround and had no DGX to deliver.

text: Lisa Su, who became AMD CEO in 2014, is reported to be what to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang?
explanation: Multiple profiles report Su and Huang are relatives through Taiwanese families: Su's mother and Huang are first cousins, so Su and Huang are first cousins once removed. His sister is the tempting miss because the family link is real, but the reported relationship is a cousin link, not a sibling one.

text: Which Microsoft CEO published the memoir Hit Refresh in 2017 about transforming the company?
explanation: Nadella wrote Hit Refresh in 2017, three years after succeeding Ballmer, describing the shift to cloud and empathy in leadership. Ballmer is the tempting miss because he was CEO just before, but he left in 2014 and never wrote about the cloud turnaround.

text: Which company grew out of the online bank X.com that Elon Musk co-founded in 1999?
explanation: Musk founded X.com in 1999, it merged with Confinity in 2000 and was renamed PayPal in 2001 before eBay bought it. Tesla is the tempting miss because Musk is its public face, but he joined Tesla in 2004 as an investor, long after X.com became PayPal.

text: Who co-founded Facebook in a Harvard dorm room in 2004?
explanation: Zuckerberg launched thefacebook.com in February 2004 with Dustin Moskovitz, Eduardo Saverin and others before dropping out. Jack Dorsey is the tempting miss because he founded another social network, but his was Twitter in 2006, not Facebook.

text: Who led the DeepMind team behind AlphaGo's 2016 victory over Lee Sedol?
explanation: Silver led the reinforcement learning work behind AlphaGo and later AlphaZero, combining search with deep networks trained by self-play. Hassabis is the tempting miss because he co-founded DeepMind and was the public face of the match, but the AlphaGo papers list Silver as the lead researcher.

text: Who was the first author of OpenAI's 2021 CLIP paper on learning vision from language?
explanation: Radford led CLIP, which trained on 400 million image-text pairs and enabled zero-shot image classification without labeled data. Sutskever is the tempting miss because he led much of OpenAI's early research, but by 2021 he was focused on alignment and was not on the CLIP author list.

text: Who created the Keras deep-learning library in 2015 while working at Google?
explanation: Chollet released Keras in 2015 as a friendly front end for neural nets, and it later became the high-level API inside TensorFlow. Howard is the tempting miss because he built fast.ai on top of similar ideas, but his library came later and was aimed at courses, not as a TensorFlow API.

text: Who co-founded fast.ai with Rachel Thomas in 2016 to make deep learning accessible?
explanation: Howard and Thomas launched fast.ai in 2016 with free courses and software that put practical training ahead of theory. Ng is the tempting miss because his Coursera courses taught millions, but his platform was Deeplearning.ai, not fast.ai.

text: Who was the first author of OpenAI's 2020 Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models paper?
explanation: Kaplan's 2020 paper showed loss falls predictably with model size, data and compute, which set off the race to scale. Amodei is the tempting miss because he was a senior author and later cited the laws when founding Anthropic, but Kaplan led the analysis.

source.label: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models on arXiv

text: Which Anthropic researcher led early work on model character and the 2022 Constitutional AI approach?
explanation: Askell drove Anthropic's work on shaping Claude's character and co-authored the Constitutional AI paper that replaced some human feedback with AI feedback. Leike is the tempting miss because he later led superalignment work, but in 2022 he was still at OpenAI, not on the Constitutional AI team.

text: Who co-led OpenAI's Superalignment team with Ilya Sutskever in 2023 and resigned in May 2024 to join Anthropic?
explanation: Leike ran Superalignment with Sutskever to study how to control future superintelligent systems, then left saying he disagreed with OpenAI's priorities. Schulman is the tempting miss because he was another senior alignment researcher who later moved to Anthropic, but he never led Superalignment.

text: Which OpenAI co-founder led post-training for ChatGPT and left OpenAI in August 2024 for Anthropic?
explanation: Schulman co-founded OpenAI in 2015 and ran the reinforcement learning work that turned GPT into ChatGPT. Brockman is the tempting miss because he is the other co-founder who stayed visible as president, but he never led ChatGPT post-training and did not leave for Anthropic.

text: Which OpenAI president and co-founder had previously been CTO of Stripe?
explanation: Brockman joined Stripe as CTO in 2013, then left to co-found OpenAI in 2015 and run its engineering as president. Altman is the tempting miss because he is the public CEO, but he came from Y Combinator, not Stripe.

text: Who co-founded the Future of Life Institute in 2014 and wrote Life 3.0 in 2017?
explanation: Tegmark, an MIT cosmologist, started FLI with Jaan Tallinn and wrote Life 3.0 about stages of life with AI. Bostrom is the tempting miss because his 2014 book Superintelligence defined the same debate, but he never founded FLI.

text: Which Skype co-founder co-founded the Future of Life Institute and Cambridge's Centre for the Study of Existential Risk?
explanation: Tallinn helped build Skype, then used the proceeds to fund FLI in 2014 and CSER with Huw Price and others. Zennstrom is the tempting miss because he was the better-known Skype co-founder, but the safety institutes were Tallinn's project.

text: Which researcher, with Andrew Barto, won the 2024 Turing Award for reinforcement learning?
explanation: Sutton and Barto wrote Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction in 1998 and shared the 2024 Turing Award for the field. Barto is the tempting miss because he shares the prize and the book, but the question asks for his co-author, and Silver was their intellectual successor at DeepMind, not the co-winner.

text: Who won the 2011 Turing Award for work on Bayesian networks and causal reasoning?
explanation: Pearl's work on probabilistic reasoning and do-calculus gave AI a formal language for cause and effect, recognized by the 2011 Turing Award. Hinton is the tempting miss because he later won the same prize in 2018 for deep learning, but his award was seven years after Pearl's.

text: Who co-authored the 1969 book Perceptrons with Seymour Papert?
explanation: Minsky and Papert's 1969 book showed limits of single-layer perceptrons, which helped freeze neural-net funding for a decade. McCarthy is the tempting miss because he co-organized Dartmouth with Minsky, but Perceptrons was Minsky and Papert's critique, not his.

text: Who founded Stability AI in 2019 and released Stable Diffusion in 2022?
explanation: Mostaque founded Stability AI in London in 2019 and funded the Stable Diffusion release that made open image models mainstream in 2022. Holz is the tempting miss because he founded Midjourney the same year image models broke out, but his tool stayed closed while Stability open-sourced its weights.

text: Which Runway co-founder has served as its CEO since its founding in 2018?
explanation: Valenzuela co-founded Runway in New York in 2018 with Germanidis and Matamala and stayed as CEO through the Gen-2 video push. Germanidis is the tempting miss because he is also a co-founder, but he serves in a research role rather than as CEO.

text: Which artist won the 2022 Colorado State Fair digital-art prize with the Midjourney work Theatre d'Opera Spatial?
explanation: Allen entered the Midjourney image in 2022 and the win sparked the first mainstream debate over whether AI art counts as art. Eldagsen is the tempting miss because he also made headlines for AI art in 2023, but he refused the Sony prize rather than winning in Colorado.

text: Which 2023 viral track used AI-cloned voices of Drake and The Weeknd and was pulled from streaming?
explanation: The anonymous ghostwriter released Heart on My Sleeve in April 2023 with cloned Drake and Weeknd vocals, and labels had it removed within days. Taylor Made Freestyle is the tempting miss because Drake himself used AI Tupac and Snoop voices on it in 2024, but that was an official diss track, not the 2023 clone stunt. Grimes responded by offering 50 percent royalties to anyone cloning her voice.

text: Which former MIT researcher has hosted the Lex Fridman Podcast since 2018 with long interviews of AI scientists?
explanation: Fridman, who worked on autonomous vehicles at MIT, started the podcast in 2018 and became the default long-form interviewer for AI leaders. Dwarkesh Patel is the tempting miss because he also interviews the same researchers at length, but his show started later and grew out of his blog, not MIT research.

text: Who became president of the Signal Foundation in 2022 after researching AI and labor?
explanation: Whittaker organized against Project Maven at Google, then took over Signal in 2022 to run private messaging at scale. Crawford is the tempting miss because she wrote Atlas of AI in 2021 about the same extractive costs, but she stayed in research rather than running Signal.

text: Who founded the Chinese AI startup 01.AI in 2023 after leading Google China?
explanation: Lee ran Google China and later Sinovation Ventures before founding 01.AI in 2023 to build open Chinese language models. Liang Wenfeng is the tempting miss because he founded the other famous Chinese open-weights lab, but his company is DeepSeek, not 01.AI.

text: Who founded TSMC in Taiwan in 1987 and pioneered the foundry model of making chips for others?
explanation: Chang founded TSMC in 1987 after decades at Texas Instruments, betting that design and manufacturing should split. Huang is the tempting miss because Nvidia is TSMC's most famous customer, but he buys wafers from Chang's company rather than founding it.

text: Which chip architect led development of AMD's Zen, Apple's A4 and A5, and Tesla's self-driving chip?
explanation: Keller led AMD's K8 and later Zen teams, did two stints at Apple on the A4 and A5, then ran Tesla Autopilot hardware before moving to Intel and Tenstorrent. Faggin is the tempting miss because he designed the Intel 4004, but his landmark work was fifty years before Keller's Zen comeback.

text: Who was the first PhD student of AI researcher Andrew Ng?
explanation: Abbeel earned his PhD at Stanford under Andrew Ng, who was then a first-year professor, and later became a Berkeley professor and co-founded Covariant. Fei-Fei Li is the tempting miss because she is also a Stanford AI professor who worked with Ng, but she was not his first doctoral student.

text: Which UC Berkeley professor developed guided policy search for robotic control?
explanation: Levine, a Berkeley professor, developed guided policy search to train deep networks for complex robotic tasks. Abbeel is the tempting miss because he advised Levine's postdoc and also works on robot learning, but guided policy search is Levine's contribution.

text: Which researcher introduced Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) in 2017?
explanation: Finn and colleagues at Berkeley introduced MAML, which trains models to adapt quickly to new tasks with few examples. Abbeel is the tempting miss as a co-author and her doctoral advisor, but Finn led the work.

text: Which Stanford professor founded the Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM)?
explanation: Liang founded CRFM at Stanford to study the development and evaluation of foundation models. Fei-Fei Li is the tempting miss as a famous Stanford AI professor, but CRFM is Liang's initiative.

text: Which Stanford computer scientist won a MacArthur 'genius' grant in 2015?
explanation: Ré won the MacArthur Fellowship in 2015 for work on big data analysis and co-founded Lattice.io, later acquired by Apple. Liang is the tempting miss as another Stanford professor, but the MacArthur went to Ré.

text: Who created the Apache Spark data processing engine?
explanation: Zaharia created Apache Spark while at UC Berkeley as a faster alternative to MapReduce. Stoica is the tempting miss because he co-founded Databricks with Zaharia, but Spark itself was Zaharia's project.

text: Which UC Berkeley professor co-founded Anyscale, the company behind the Ray framework?
explanation: Stoica co-founded Anyscale with the original developers of Ray. Zaharia is the tempting miss because he also co-founded Databricks with Stoica, but Anyscale and Ray are Stoica's venture.

text: Who created the Python programming language?
explanation: Van Rossum created Python in 1989 as a hobby project over Christmas. Oliphant is the tempting miss because he created NumPy, a core Python library, but not the language itself.
